countries.name: Albania
countries.summary: Albania's Riviera (Ksamil, Himarë, Dhërmi) is a June–September beach destination, best in June and September. The Accursed Mountains (Theth, Valbona) open for hiking from June. The UNESCO towns of Berat and Gjirokastër are lovely in spring and autumn. It's one of Europe's best-value countries.
countries.splitReason: Albania is small, and the Riviera, the cities and the Alps share one Mediterranean-continental calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Tirana, the Albanian Riviera, Berat, Gjirokastër, Shkodër and the Accursed Mountains.

best.why: Uncrowded Riviera beaches, with the Theth and Valbona hikes opening in June.
A warm sea and golden mountains.

worst.why: Rainy, with mountain roads (Theth) snowbound.

shoulder.why: Spring blossom, with a cool sea.

risks.note: The road to Theth is closed by snow.

prices.notes: Great value, though Ksamil prices rise sharply in August.

countries.name: Andorra
countries.summary: Andorra is primarily a ski destination (Grandvalira, Vallnord) from December to April, with a summer hiking season from late June to September. The rest of the year it's mainly duty-free shopping.
countries.splitReason: Andorra is a small Pyrenean principality with one mountain climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Andorra la Vella, Grandvalira and Vallnord-Pal Arinsal.

best.why: Ski season with plenty of sunshine.
Pyrenean hiking and lakes.

worst.why: Between seasons, with little to do.

shoulder.why: The ski season opens, with holiday crowds.

prices.notes: Ski packages are cheaper than in the Alps.

countries.name: Austria
countries.summary: Austria has two peak seasons: skiing in Tyrol and Salzburgerland (December–March) and summer in the Alps and on the lakes (June–September). Vienna's coffee houses, opera and Christmas markets work all year. November and late April to May are quiet in-between months in the mountains.
countries.splitReason: Vienna and the Alpine provinces share one central-European calendar: alpine winters for skiing and warm summers for lakes and hiking.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The whole country: Vienna, Salzburg, Innsbruck and Tyrol, Hallstatt and the Salzkammergut, the Wachau and the ski resorts.

best.why: Prime ski season in Tyrol and Salzburgerland after the holidays.
Alpine meadows, warming lakes and festivals.
Golden autumn, wine taverns (Heurigen) and hiking.

worst.why: A grey in-between month: ski lifts are closed and the hiking season is over.

shoulder.why: Christmas markets and the ski season opening, with peak prices at Christmas.
Spring skiing on the glaciers; valleys turning green.
The Salzburg Festival, busy mountains and afternoon storms.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas markets
recurringHolidays.effect: Vienna and Salzburg are busy.

recurringHolidays.name: Salzburg Festival
recurringHolidays.effect: Salzburg hotels at peak prices.

prices.notes: Ski passes cost €60–75 a day. Hallstatt limits tourist buses, so stay overnight to enjoy it quietly.

countries.name: Belarus
countries.summary: Many governments advise against travel to Belarus, so check current advice. Climatically, late spring and summer suit Minsk, Mir and Nesvizh castles and the primeval Białowieża Forest. Winters are long and cold.
countries.splitReason: Belarus is flat, with one continental calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Minsk, Brest and the Białowieża Forest, Grodno, and the Mir and Nesvizh castles.

best.why: Long, green days for the castles and forest.
Warm late summer with the harvest beginning.

worst.why: A long, cold, grey winter.

prices.notes: Visa rules and international card acceptance change often, so check before going.

countries.name: Belgium
countries.summary: Belgium's cities (Brussels, Bruges, Ghent, Antwerp) are year-round destinations with a mild, rainy climate. Late spring to early autumn is most pleasant, and Advent brings atmospheric Christmas markets.
countries.splitReason: Belgium is small, with one maritime climate; the Ardennes are just slightly colder.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The whole country: Brussels, Bruges, Ghent, Antwerp, Leuven and the Ardennes.

best.why: Warm days and terrace beers in Ghent and Bruges.
Mild, with crowds thinning.

worst.why: Grey, wet, cold and short days.

shoulder.why: Dark but festive: Christmas markets in Brussels and Bruges.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas markets
recurringHolidays.effect: Brussels Winter Wonders; Bruges is busy at weekends.

prices.notes: Bruges is pricey at weekends, while Ghent and Leuven are better value.

countries.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
countries.summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina is best in late spring and early autumn. Summer is hot in Mostar (38 °C) and busy at the Stari Most bridge. Winter brings cheap skiing at Jahorina and Bjelašnica, but also smog in Sarajevo on still days.
countries.splitReason: Bosnia and Herzegovina is small, and Sarajevo, Mostar and the mountains share one calendar; Mostar is simply hotter.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Sarajevo, Mostar, Blagaj, the Kravice falls, Jajce and the Olympic mountains.

best.why: Green valleys, the Kravice falls flowing and comfortable sightseeing.
Golden autumn days in the valleys and old towns.

worst.why: Wet and foggy, with the mountain resorts not yet open.

shoulder.why: Skiing at Jahorina and Bjelašnica, with Sarajevo smog on still days.
Mostar is hot (38 °C) and crowded at Stari Most.

prices.notes: Great value. Mostar is busiest with day-trippers from Dubrovnik at midday.

countries.name: Bulgaria
countries.summary: Bulgaria combines a Black Sea beach coast (best June–September), the Rila and Pirin mountains (hiking in summer, cheap skiing at Bansko from December to March) and historic Sofia, Plovdiv and Veliko Tarnovo. Late May to early June is rose-harvest time in the Valley of Roses.

regions.name: Black Sea Coast
regions.description: Varna, Burgas, Sunny Beach, Nesebar, Sozopol and Golden Sands.

best.why: A warming sea and long sunny days before the crowds.
The sea still warm, with resorts quieter.

worst.why: Resorts are closed and it's grey and windy.

shoulder.why: Resorts are reopening and the sea is cool.
Peak season: Sunny Beach is packed and hot.

recurringHolidays.name: Rose Festival (Kazanlak)
recurringHolidays.effect: The rose-picking and festival in the Valley of Roses.

prices.notes: Sunny Beach is a party resort, while Sozopol and Nesebar are quieter.

regions.name: Sofia, Plovdiv & the Mountains
regions.description: Sofia, Plovdiv, Rila Monastery and the Seven Lakes, Veliko Tarnovo, Bansko and the Pirin, Borovets and Koprivshtitsa.

best.why: The rose harvest in the Valley of Roses (late May to early June), with mountain trails opening.
Warm autumn and clear mountain views.

worst.why: Mud season: skiing is over and the high trails are closed.

shoulder.why: Skiing at Bansko and Borovets (good value).
Hot cities, but perfect for Rila and Pirin hikes.

recurringHolidays.name: Rose Festival (Kazanlak)
recurringHolidays.effect: The rose-picking and festival in the Valley of Roses.

prices.notes: Bansko is among Europe's cheapest ski resorts.

countries.name: Croatia
countries.summary: Croatia's Adriatic coast and islands are a May-to-October destination, best in June and September. July–August means peak crowds in Dubrovnik and Hvar and full ferries, and most island hotels shut in winter. Inland, Zagreb and the Plitvice Lakes are good from spring to autumn, and Zagreb's Advent is among Europe's best Christmas markets.

regions.name: Adriatic Coast & Islands
regions.description: Dubrovnik, Split, Hvar, Brač, Korčula, Vis, Zadar, Šibenik and Krka, Makarska, Istria (Rovinj, Pula) and Kvarner.

best.why: Warm sea, sunny days and island ferries running before the crowds.
The sea at 23–25 °C, calmer old towns and the grape harvest.

worst.why: Cruise crowds in Dubrovnik, peak prices and full ferries.
Island hotels and ferries are limited, with bora winds and rain.

shoulder.why: Spring wildflowers, with a cool sea.
Very warm sea, with crowds easing.

risks.note: Bora gales close bridges and ferries.

recurringHolidays.name: Assumption Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak holiday crowds on the coast.

prices.notes: Dubrovnik and Hvar are the priciest. Book ferries and catamarans ahead in summer.

regions.name: Zagreb & Inland Croatia
regions.description: Zagreb, the Plitvice Lakes, Rastoke, Varaždin and Slavonia.

best.why: The Plitvice waterfalls in full flow, with everything green.
Autumn colours at Plitvice and fewer crowds.

worst.why: Cold and grey; Plitvice's upper-lake paths can close with snow and ice.

shoulder.why: Advent in Zagreb, one of Europe's best Christmas markets.
Hot and busy, with Plitvice crowds peaking.

recurringHolidays.name: Assumption Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak holiday crowds on the coast.

prices.notes: Buy Plitvice tickets online for a time slot in summer.

countries.name: Cyprus
countries.summary: Cyprus is one of Europe's sunniest places, with 340 sunny days a year. The beach season runs from May to early November, with the sea at 25–27 °C in autumn. July and August are very hot, especially inland in Nicosia. Winter is mild (17–19 °C) on the coast, with snow up in the Troodos.
countries.splitReason: Cyprus is a small island with one Mediterranean climate; the Troodos mountains are cooler, with skiing from January to March.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The whole island: Limassol, Paphos, Larnaca, Ayia Napa, Nicosia, the Troodos mountains and the north (Kyrenia).

best.why: Wildflowers and warm days, with the sea warming.
The sea stays at 25–27 °C into November.

worst.why: Very hot (35 °C+ inland in Nicosia), with peak crowds.

shoulder.why: A mild, sunny 17–19 °C winter, with snow in the Troodos (January–February).

risks.note: Forest fires in the Troodos foothills.

prices.notes: Hiring a car is essential. Crossing to the north is easy at the Nicosia checkpoints.

countries.name: Czechia
countries.summary: Prague and the Czech towns are lovely in late spring and early autumn. Summer brings huge crowds on Charles Bridge, and Advent brings beautiful but busy Christmas markets. January to early March is cold and grey.
countries.splitReason: Czechia is small, with one central-European climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The whole country: Prague, Český Krumlov, Karlovy Vary, Kutná Hora, Brno and Bohemian Switzerland.

best.why: Blooming gardens and warm days before the summer crowds.
A golden autumn and the wine harvest in Moravia.

worst.why: Cold and grey (−3 to 3 °C).

shoulder.why: Prague's Christmas markets: beautiful but crowded.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas markets
recurringHolidays.effect: The Old Town Square and Wenceslas Square are busy.

prices.notes: Prague's old town is pricier than the rest of the country. Český Krumlov is best visited overnight.

countries.name: Denmark
countries.summary: Denmark is at its best from late spring to late summer: long light days, harbour swims in Copenhagen, Roskilde Festival and cycling. Autumn and winter are dark and windy, though Tivoli's Christmas market and 'hygge' make December special.
countries.splitReason: Denmark is small and flat, with one maritime climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The whole country: Copenhagen, Aarhus, Odense, Skagen, Bornholm and Legoland, plus the Faroe Islands.

best.why: Long light days, harbour swimming, Roskilde Festival and cycling.

worst.why: Dark, grey and windy.

shoulder.why: Hygge season with Tivoli's Christmas market, but dark by 3:45 pm.

recurringHolidays.name: Roskilde Festival
recurringHolidays.effect: Northern Europe's biggest music festival.

recurringHolidays.name: Tivoli Christmas
recurringHolidays.effect: Copenhagen is busy at weekends.

prices.notes: Expensive, but the Copenhagen Card and free harbour swimming help.

countries.name: Estonia
countries.summary: Estonia's medieval Tallinn and its islands are best in summer, with white nights and festivals. Winters are long and dark, but Tallinn's Christmas market is one of Europe's prettiest.
countries.splitReason: Estonia is small and flat, with one Baltic climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Tallinn, Tartu, Pärnu, Saaremaa and Lahemaa National Park.

best.why: White nights, a buzzing medieval old town and the islands (Saaremaa).

worst.why: Dark, cold and slushy.

shoulder.why: Dark, but Tallinn's Christmas market is magical.

prices.notes: Tallinn is busy with cruise day-trippers in summer.

countries.name: Finland
countries.summary: Finland's south (Helsinki and the Lakeland) is best in the white nights of June to August, with saunas, lakes and archipelago islands. Finnish Lapland is the winter star: snow from November to April, Santa Claus Village at Christmas, and northern lights with daylight returning from January to March. Ruska autumn colours arrive in September.

regions.name: Helsinki & the Lakeland
regions.description: Helsinki, Porvoo, the Turku archipelago, Tampere and the Lakeland (Savonlinna, Saimaa).

best.why: White nights, lakeside cottages and saunas, and archipelago islands.

worst.why: Dark, slushy and cold.

shoulder.why: Lengthening days, with snow lingering into April.

recurringHolidays.name: Midsummer (Juhannus)
recurringHolidays.effect: Finns head to lakeside cottages; cities empty and shops close.

prices.notes: Lakeside cottages (mökki) are a great way to stay in summer.

regions.name: Finnish Lapland
regions.description: Rovaniemi and Santa Claus Village, Levi, Ylläs, Saariselkä and Inari.

best.why: Northern lights with daylight returning: huskies, snowmobiles and glass igloos.
Midnight sun, hiking and canoeing.

worst.why: Dark and often without snow, with many activities not yet running.
Snowmelt slush, with little to do.

shoulder.why: The Christmas peak at Santa Claus Village (very expensive) during polar night.
Ruska colours and the first auroras.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas in Lapland
recurringHolidays.effect: Rovaniemi prices triple; book a year ahead.

recurringHolidays.name: Midsummer (Juhannus)
recurringHolidays.effect: Finns head to lakeside cottages; cities empty and shops close.

prices.notes: Christmas week is extremely expensive. Late February to March offers better value and more daylight.

countries.name: France
countries.summary: Mainland France ranges from the mild, damp Atlantic north-west and the continental east to the Alps, with Europe's best ski season from January to March, and the sunny Mediterranean south. Late spring and September are the best all-round times. France's long holiday from mid-July to late August jams the roads and fills the coasts. Overseas France adds Caribbean islands (best December–May), Réunion and New Caledonia in the southern hemisphere (best in the austral winter), and French Polynesia (best May–October).

regions.name: Paris & Northern France
regions.description: Paris and Île-de-France, Normandy, Brittany, the Loire Valley, Champagne, Burgundy, Alsace, Lyon and Lille.

best.why: Long days at 20–24 °C with gardens and café terraces, fresh Loire châteaux and the Normandy coast.
La rentrée: warm and golden, with the cultural season and grape harvests in Champagne and Burgundy.

worst.why: Many Parisian restaurants shut for the holidays, queues peak, and heatwaves are possible.

shoulder.why: Short grey days (5–8 °C), but Christmas lights, the Alsace markets and the museum season.
Changeable spring with blossom and showers.
Warm and busy, with Bastille Day.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas markets
recurringHolidays.effect: Strasbourg and Colmar hotels are full.

recurringHolidays.name: Bastille Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Fireworks; central Paris is crowded and closed off.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter weekend
recurringHolidays.effect: School holidays and busy roads.

recurringHolidays.name: French summer holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Coasts and campsites are full and motorways jammed ('bouchons').

prices.notes: Paris is expensive and there's a tourist tax; Lyon and the regions are cheaper. Book the Louvre online.

regions.name: French Alps & Pyrenees
regions.description: Chamonix and Mont Blanc, Annecy, Val d'Isère and Tignes, the Three Valleys (Courchevel, Méribel, Val Thorens), Grenoble and the Pyrenees.

best.why: Prime ski season with reliable snow (avoid the February school holidays).
Alpine summer: the Tour du Mont Blanc, Lake Annecy and wildflower meadows.

worst.why: Lifts closed, high trails still snowy and many hotels shut.
Between seasons: resorts shut and grey, with no snow yet.

shoulder.why: The ski season opens; Christmas is the peak-price week.
Valleys are green while the high passes open.
Golden larches, with lifts and huts closing.

risks.note: Off-piste avalanche danger; check the bulletins.

recurringHolidays.name: French ski school holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Resorts are at peak prices and full.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter weekend
recurringHolidays.effect: School holidays and busy roads.

recurringHolidays.name: French summer holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Coasts and campsites are full and motorways jammed ('bouchons').

prices.notes: Courchevel and Val d'Isère are luxury-priced. Lift passes cost €60–75 a day.

regions.name: Provence, Riviera & Corsica
regions.description: Provence (Avignon, Aix, the Luberon, Arles and the Camargue), the Côte d'Azur (Nice, Cannes, Antibes, Saint-Tropez), Marseille, Montpellier and Corsica.

best.why: The lavender begins (mid-June) and days are 22–26 °C with the sea warming.
A warm sea, the wine harvest and fewer crowds.

worst.why: Peak French holidays: gridlock on the coast, peak hotel prices, and mistral winds raising the wildfire risk.

shoulder.why: Mild, sunny Riviera winters (13 °C), the Menton Lemon Festival in February and a quiet Provence.

risks.note: Forest fires in Provence and Corsica; some massifs close to hikers.

recurringHolidays.name: Cannes Film Festival
recurringHolidays.effect: Cannes hotel prices increase fivefold.

recurringHolidays.name: Nice Carnival
recurringHolidays.effect: Flower battles and parades.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter weekend
recurringHolidays.effect: School holidays and busy roads.

recurringHolidays.name: French summer holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Coasts and campsites are full and motorways jammed ('bouchons').

prices.notes: Saint-Tropez and Cannes are luxury territory. Inland Provence and Corsica's interior are better value.

regions.name: South-West France
regions.description: Bordeaux and its vineyards, the Dordogne, the Basque coast (Biarritz), Arcachon, Toulouse, Carcassonne and Lourdes.

best.why: Warm and green: châteaux and Dordogne caves before the crowds.
The grape harvest (vendanges) and the surf season on the Basque coast.

worst.why: A damp, grey Atlantic winter, with many Dordogne sights closed.

shoulder.why: Hot (27–32 °C) and busy, with great beaches at Biarritz and Arcachon.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter weekend
recurringHolidays.effect: School holidays and busy roads.

recurringHolidays.name: French summer holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Coasts and campsites are full and motorways jammed ('bouchons').

prices.notes: Wine-estate stays are popular; book harvest-season tours early.

regions.name: French Caribbean
regions.description: Guadeloupe, Martinique, Saint-Martin and Saint-Barthélemy.

best.why: The dry season (carême): sunny with trade-wind breezes, and Carnival in February or March.

worst.why: Peak hurricane season; it's humid and many hotels close in September.

shoulder.why: Hot and showery, with the hurricane risk rising.

risks.note: Peak risk from mid-August to mid-October.

recurringHolidays.name: Carnival
recurringHolidays.effect: Street parades in Pointe-à-Pitre and Fort-de-France.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter weekend
recurringHolidays.effect: School holidays and busy roads.

recurringHolidays.name: French summer holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Coasts and campsites are full and motorways jammed ('bouchons').

prices.notes: Saint-Barthélemy is ultra-luxury. Guadeloupe gîtes are good value.

regions.name: Réunion & Mayotte
regions.description: Réunion (Piton de la Fournaise and the cirques of Mafate, Cilaos and Salazie) and Mayotte, in the Indian Ocean.

best.why: The dry austral winter: perfect hiking in the cirques, volcano treks and whale-watching (July–October).

worst.why: Peak cyclone season, with torrential rain closing trails.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter weekend
recurringHolidays.effect: School holidays and busy roads.

recurringHolidays.name: French summer holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Coasts and campsites are full and motorways jammed ('bouchons').

prices.notes: Mafate is reachable only on foot or by helicopter, so book gîtes ahead.

regions.name: French Polynesia
regions.description: Tahiti, Moorea, Bora Bora, Rangiroa and the Tuamotus, and the Marquesas.

best.why: The dry austral winter: sunny and less humid, with humpback whales (July–October) and the Heiva festival in July.

worst.why: Wet season with heavy downpours; cyclones are rare but possible.

recurringHolidays.name: Heiva i Tahiti
recurringHolidays.effect: The Polynesian dance festival; Papeete is busy.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter weekend
recurringHolidays.effect: School holidays and busy roads.

recurringHolidays.name: French summer holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Coasts and campsites are full and motorways jammed ('bouchons').

prices.notes: Overwater bungalows cost $800 a night or more, and family pensions are far cheaper. Island-hopping air passes save money.

regions.name: New Caledonia
regions.description: Nouméa, the Île des Pins and the Loyalty Islands, around the world's largest lagoon.

best.why: Dry and sunny at 25–28 °C with a calm lagoon.

worst.why: Cyclone season, with heavy rain.

shoulder.why: A cool, dry austral winter (23 °C), with humpback whales from July.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter weekend
recurringHolidays.effect: School holidays and busy roads.

recurringHolidays.name: French summer holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Coasts and campsites are full and motorways jammed ('bouchons').

prices.notes: Expensive because nearly everything is imported. The CFP franc is pegged to the euro.

regions.name: French Guiana
regions.description: Cayenne, the Kourou space centre, the Îles du Salut and the Amazon rainforest.

best.why: Dry season: rocket launches at Kourou, the Îles du Salut and rainforest lodges.

worst.why: The wettest months, with 450–560 mm of rain.

shoulder.why: Rains with a short drier spell in March (the 'petit été'), plus Carnival from January to February.

recurringHolidays.name: Guianese Carnival
recurringHolidays.effect: Weekly street parades in Cayenne.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter weekend
recurringHolidays.effect: School holidays and busy roads.

recurringHolidays.name: French summer holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Coasts and campsites are full and motorways jammed ('bouchons').

prices.notes: Book launch viewing at Kourou in advance. It uses the euro, and prices are high.

countries.name: Germany
countries.summary: Germany is a four-season country. Late spring and early autumn are ideal for cities, Rhine cruises and the Romantic Road. Summer is warm but changeable, with storms. September–October brings Oktoberfest and wine festivals, and Advent's Christmas markets are magical despite the cold. January to March is grey everywhere except on the ski slopes.
countries.splitReason: Germany's continental-maritime climate follows one calendar from the North Sea to Bavaria, with the Alps adding winter sports.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The whole country: Berlin, Munich and Bavaria, Hamburg, the Rhine and Mosel, the Black Forest, Dresden, the Bavarian Alps and the North and Baltic coasts.

best.why: Beer gardens, Rhine and Mosel cruises and 20–24 °C days.
Wine-harvest festivals, Oktoberfest (late September) and golden forests.

worst.why: Cold, grey and short days (−2 to 5 °C), with the Christmas markets over.

shoulder.why: The Advent Christmas markets: magical but cold.
The warmest weeks, with busy school holidays and thunderstorms.

recurringHolidays.name: Oktoberfest (Munich)
recurringHolidays.effect: Munich hotels triple in price; book a year ahead.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas markets
recurringHolidays.effect: Nuremberg, Dresden and Cologne are packed at weekends.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter
recurringHolidays.effect: Long weekend; attractions are busy.

prices.notes: Good value for Western Europe. The Deutschlandticket covers regional trains for a monthly fee.

countries.name: Greece
countries.summary: Greece has hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters. The islands are a May-to-October destination: most hotels and tavernas close from November to March, and the meltemi wind blows strongly in July–August. Athens and the mainland ruins are best in spring and autumn, since summer heatwaves can close the Acropolis at midday. Greek Orthodox Easter and the mid-August holiday are the domestic peaks.

regions.name: Athens & the Mainland
regions.description: Athens, Delphi, Meteora, the Peloponnese (Nafplio, Mycenae, Olympia, Monemvasia), Thessaloniki, Halkidiki and Mt Olympus.

best.why: Warm 20–28 °C: the Acropolis, Delphi and Meteora before the heat, with wildflowers in the Peloponnese.
A warm sea and comfortable conditions at the ruins.

worst.why: Athens heatwaves of 35–40 °C close the Acropolis at midday, with crowds on top.

shoulder.why: A mild, wet winter: quiet sites and cheap hotels.

risks.note: Heatwaves close archaeological sites at midday.
Forest fires around Attica and the Peloponnese.

recurringHolidays.name: Greek Orthodox Easter
recurringHolidays.effect: The most important holiday: ferries and hotels are full.

recurringHolidays.name: Dormition (Panagia)
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak Greek holidays: ferries sell out.

prices.notes: From April to October the Acropolis is busiest from 10 am to 2 pm, so book a timed ticket for 8 am.

regions.name: Cyclades & Dodecanese
regions.description: Santorini, Mykonos, Naxos, Paros, Milos, Ios and Sifnos, plus the Dodecanese (Rhodes, Kos, Patmos).

best.why: Warm, sunny days with a warming sea; island ferries are running and July's crowds haven't arrived.
A warm sea, softer light and thinning crowds.

worst.why: Peak crowds and prices (Santorini cruise days), and strong meltemi winds cancel ferries.
Most hotels and tavernas close and ferries are limited.

shoulder.why: The islands are waking up, but the sea is still cool.
Still busy, with a warm sea.

risks.note: Meltemi gales of force 6–8 cancel ferries and make some beaches unswimmable.

recurringHolidays.name: Greek Orthodox Easter
recurringHolidays.effect: The most important holiday: ferries and hotels are full.

recurringHolidays.name: Dormition (Panagia)
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak Greek holidays: ferries sell out.

prices.notes: Santorini caldera and Mykonos hotels are luxury-priced in summer. Naxos and Paros are better value.

regions.name: Crete
regions.description: Heraklion and Knossos, Chania, Rethymno, Elafonisi and Balos beaches, the Samaria Gorge and Elounda.

best.why: Wildflowers, the Samaria Gorge reopening (May) and a warm sea.
The sea at 24 °C and a long season into October.

worst.why: Hot, crowded and at peak prices.

shoulder.why: A mild, wet winter: many resorts are closed, but the cities stay lively.

recurringHolidays.name: Greek Orthodox Easter
recurringHolidays.effect: The most important holiday: ferries and hotels are full.

recurringHolidays.name: Dormition (Panagia)
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak Greek holidays: ferries sell out.

prices.notes: Great value, especially western Crete. Hire a car to explore.

regions.name: Ionian Islands
regions.description: Corfu, Kefalonia, Zakynthos (Navagio), Lefkada, Ithaca and Paxos.

best.why: Lush, green islands, warm days and a warming sea.
A warm sea and calm conditions.

worst.why: Peak crowds and prices.
Greece's wettest islands, with the resorts shut.

shoulder.why: Spring flowers, with a cool sea.

recurringHolidays.name: Greek Orthodox Easter
recurringHolidays.effect: The most important holiday: ferries and hotels are full.

recurringHolidays.name: Dormition (Panagia)
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak Greek holidays: ferries sell out.

prices.notes: Corfu is busy with UK package tourism. Paxos and Ithaca are quieter.

countries.name: Hungary
countries.summary: Budapest is great in spring and autumn. Summers are hot (30 °C+), when Lake Balaton beaches and festivals like Sziget are the draw. Winters are cold and grey, but the thermal baths and Christmas markets shine.
countries.splitReason: Hungary is a compact, flat country with one continental climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Budapest, Lake Balaton, Eger, Tokaj, Pécs and the Danube Bend.

best.why: Warm, blossoming Budapest and terrace season.
Harvest festivals in Eger and Tokaj, with comfortable city days.

worst.why: Cold, foggy and grey (−3 to 3 °C), though the thermal baths shine.

shoulder.why: Christmas markets and the thermal baths.
Hot (28–33 °C), with the Lake Balaton season and the Sziget festival.

recurringHolidays.name: Sziget Festival
recurringHolidays.effect: One of Europe's biggest music festivals; Budapest hotels peak.

recurringHolidays.name: St Stephen's Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Fireworks over the Danube.

prices.notes: Good value. The famous baths (Széchenyi, Gellért) cost €25–35.

countries.name: Iceland
countries.summary: Iceland has two seasons. Summer (June–August) brings the midnight sun, open Highland roads, puffins and the easiest Ring Road driving. Winter (October–March) is the season for northern lights and ice caves, but with 4–5 hours of daylight and storms that can close roads. Shoulder months are increasingly popular. It's one of the world's most expensive countries.
countries.splitReason: Iceland's population lives along the coast, which shares one sub-Arctic maritime calendar; the Highlands only open in summer.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The whole country: Reykjavík, the Golden Circle, the south coast, Jökulsárlón, Akureyri and Mývatn, the Westfjords and the Highlands.

best.why: Midnight sun, Highland F-roads open (from late June), puffins and the Ring Road at its easiest.

worst.why: The shortest days (4–5 hours of light) and storms that close roads; auroras are possible but skies are often cloudy.

shoulder.why: Lengthening days, auroras until mid-April and ice caves until March.
Autumn colours, the start of the northern lights season and fewer tourists.

risks.note: Storms close the Ring Road; check umferdin.is.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Bonfires and fireworks; some tours are closed.

prices.notes: Very expensive. Supermarkets (Bónus, Krónan) and camper vans help keep costs down.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.summary: Ireland is mild and green, and showers can come at any time. May, June and September bring the most settled weather and long evenings on the Wild Atlantic Way. July and August are busiest. Winter is wet and windy, though St Patrick's Day in March is a huge draw.
countries.splitReason: Ireland's mild maritime climate is similar everywhere. The west is wetter, but the seasons align.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The whole island south of Northern Ireland: Dublin, Galway, Cork, Kerry, the Cliffs of Moher and the Wild Atlantic Way.

best.why: The longest days and driest spell, with the Wild Atlantic Way at its greenest.
Settled early autumn, with fewer crowds.

worst.why: Short, wet and windy days, with some west-coast attractions closed.

shoulder.why: Spring showers, with St Patrick's Day in March.
The busiest season, at a mild 19 °C.

recurringHolidays.name: St Patrick's Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Dublin hotels triple in price.

prices.notes: Dublin is expensive, and B&Bs in the west are better value.

countries.name: Italy
countries.summary: Italy runs 1,200 km from the Alps to within sight of Africa, so its seasons shift as you go south. The north has cold, foggy winters and some of Europe's best skiing. The centre and south have hot, dry summers and mild, wetter winters, while Sicily and Sardinia have almost North African summers. Late spring and early autumn are the sweet spot nearly everywhere. The real enemy is August: heat, Ferragosto closures in the cities and beaches packed with Italian families.

regions.name: Northern Italy & Alps
regions.description: Lombardy, Piedmont, Veneto, Trentino–Alto Adige (Dolomites), Friuli, Emilia-Romagna and Liguria: Milan, Venice, Turin, Bologna, the Italian Lakes, the Dolomites and the Cinque Terre.

best.why: Warm (22–27 °C) without the summer haze. The lakes and Cinque Terre trails are fully open, mountain huts start opening from mid-June and the cities are in full swing.
Settled, golden weather: grape and truffle harvests in Piedmont, warm lake water, and Dolomite trails still open with fewer people.

worst.why: Ferragosto: many city restaurants and shops close, the coast and lakes are packed with Italian families, and the Po Valley sits at 33 °C or more with sticky humidity.
The wettest, greyest stretch. Dense fog blankets the Po Valley, Venice floods (acqua alta), and many lake hotels and mountain lifts are closed between seasons.
Christmas to Epiphany: ski resorts are fully booked at peak prices and city hotels are expensive.

shoulder.why: Prime ski season in the Dolomites and Aosta Valley at post-holiday prices. Cities are cold (0–10 °C), foggy and quiet. Watch for the Milan Fashion Week and Venice Carnival price spikes.
Spring blossom and mild 16–22 °C days, with lake ferries back on full timetables. Showers are frequent, and Easter and Milan Design Week push prices up.
Peak summer: perfect for the high Alps and the lakes, but hot (30–33 °C) and humid in Milan, Bologna and Venice.
Autumn colour and food festivals. Rainfall rises sharply from mid-October and mountain huts close.
Christmas markets in Bolzano, Merano and Trento; the ski season opens. It's cold and often foggy in the plains.

risks.note: Heatwaves in the Po Valley plains (Milan, Bologna, Verona) can reach 35–38 °C.
Afternoon storms with hail over the Alps and lakes; start mountain hikes early.
Venice acqua alta and flash floods or landslides in Liguria.
Thick Po Valley fog can delay flights and make motorway driving hazardous.
Off-piste avalanche danger; check the regional bulletins.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter week (Settimana Santa)
recurringHolidays.effect: Domestic travel surge: lake and Riviera hotels fill and prices rise about 20–30%.

recurringHolidays.name: Venice Carnival
recurringHolidays.effect: Venice hotels can double or triple; St Mark's Square is packed.

recurringHolidays.name: Milan Design Week (Salone del Mobile)
recurringHolidays.effect: Milan hotel rates triple and rooms sell out months ahead.

recurringHolidays.name: Liberation Day & May Day bridges
recurringHolidays.effect: Long 'ponte' weekends fill the lakes and Cinque Terre.

recurringHolidays.name: Ferragosto
recurringHolidays.effect: City restaurants and shops close while the coast and mountains overflow.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas to Epiphany
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak ski-resort prices with minimum-stay rules.

prices.notes: Milan hotels spike during the fashion weeks (Feb, Sep) and Design Week (Apr). Venice is the most expensive city, and Dolomites ski hotels peak at Christmas and in February.

regions.name: Central Italy
regions.description: Lazio, Tuscany, Umbria, Marche and Abruzzo: Rome, Florence, Siena, Pisa, the Chianti and Val d'Orcia countryside, Perugia and the Apennines.

best.why: Warm 20–27 °C days, wisteria in Rome and poppy-dotted Tuscan hills, and long evenings for outdoor dining. The weather is ideal for walking cities.
Grape harvest in Chianti, softer light, a still-warm sea on the Tuscan coast, and summer heat and crowds easing at the Vatican and the Uffizi.

worst.why: Heatwaves of 33–38 °C in Rome and Florence, peak queues at the major museums and Ferragosto closures. Sightseeing in the midday sun is genuinely exhausting.

shoulder.why: Mild 15–20 °C with some rain. Queues are shorter, though Easter week in Rome is very busy.
Hot (29–32 °C) but the beach season is in full swing and evenings are lovely; crowds build.
Still hot, but Italians are returning to work and the crowds are thinning.
The wettest stretch (Oct–Nov), but prices are lowest, museums are quiet and the olive oil harvest is on.

risks.note: Regional heat alerts are common; Rome and Florence can exceed 38 °C.
Fire risk on the Tuscan and Lazio coasts and hills in dry summers.
Autumn cloudbursts cause flash floods; the Arno and Tiber occasionally run high.

recurringHolidays.name: Holy Week & Easter in Rome
recurringHolidays.effect: Vatican ceremonies draw huge crowds and Rome hotels peak.

recurringHolidays.name: Palio di Siena
recurringHolidays.effect: Siena fills and hotel rates soar around the horse race.

recurringHolidays.name: Ferragosto
recurringHolidays.effect: Many family-run restaurants close and Tuscan beaches overflow.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Rome is busy with pilgrims and holidaymakers.

prices.notes: Rome and Florence city taxes add €3–7 per person per night. Tuscan agriturismi often require 3–7 night minimum stays in summer.

regions.name: Southern Italy
regions.description: Campania, Puglia, Basilicata and Calabria: Naples, Pompeii, the Amalfi Coast, Capri, Matera, Puglia's trulli and beaches, and the Calabrian coast.

best.why: Days are 23–29 °C, with lemon groves in bloom and the sea swimmable from June. Hiking the Path of the Gods is comfortable, and hotels sit below August rates.
The sea is at its warmest (24–26 °C), the grape and fig harvest is on, family crowds have gone and ferries still run full timetables.

worst.why: Peak Italian holidays: the Amalfi Coast road is gridlocked, beach clubs are sold out, room rates double and it's 33 °C or more in Naples.
Most Amalfi, Capri and Puglia resort hotels close, ferries are reduced and these are the wettest months. Naples itself still works well for culture.

shoulder.why: Mild and green with resorts reopening from Easter. The sea is still cold (15–17 °C) and there are occasional rainy spells.
Classic beach summer: hot, sunny and busy, with prices climbing towards the August peak.
The sea is still very warm and crowds are ebbing, though prices fall slowly.
Rains return and many beach hotels close from early November, but Naples and Matera are lovely and cheap.

risks.note: Inland Puglia and Basilicata can pass 40 °C.
Brush fires in Calabria, Puglia and the hills behind the Amalfi Coast.
Winter storms cancel ferries and hydrofoils to Capri and Ischia at short notice.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter
recurringHolidays.effect: Processions across the south; coastal resorts reopen and fill on Easter weekend.

recurringHolidays.name: Ferragosto
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak beach crowds and prices, with ferries and the Amalfi road at a standstill.

recurringHolidays.name: Feast of San Gennaro
recurringHolidays.effect: Naples celebrates its patron saint; the historic centre is crowded.

prices.notes: Positano and Capri are among Italy's most expensive places in summer (often €350+ a night). Puglia and Calabria are much cheaper.

regions.name: Sicily & Sardinia
regions.description: Sicily (Palermo, Catania, Taormina, Syracuse, Mount Etna, the Aeolian Islands) and Sardinia (Cagliari, Costa Smeralda, Alghero, the Gulf of Orosei).

best.why: Wildflowers, 22–28 °C and a warming sea. It's the best time to hike Etna and the Sardinian coast, and ferries and car hire are still cheap.
The warmest sea of the year (24–26 °C), harvest festivals and calm beaches with locals back at work; the sun still shines most days.

worst.why: Sardinian beaches and ferries are packed, ferry and car-hire prices hit their peak, and the inland Sicilian heat often passes 35 °C.

shoulder.why: Spring green and Easter processions. The sea is still cool (16 °C), so it's better for touring than beaches.
Hot, dry and sunny with crowds building; book ferries early.
The sea is at its warmest and the crowds are starting to fall.
Mild 14–18 °C winter days. It's great for Palermo, Syracuse and the Valley of the Temples at low prices, but beach resorts are closed.

risks.note: Scirocco winds from North Africa can push temperatures above 40 °C.
Serious fire risk in Sardinia and Sicily during dry, windy summers.
Ferries to the Aeolian and Egadi islands are frequently cancelled in winter.

recurringHolidays.name: Holy Week processions
recurringHolidays.effect: Trapani and Enna processions draw large crowds; book ahead.

recurringHolidays.name: Feast of Sant'Agata (Catania)
recurringHolidays.effect: One of the world's largest religious festivals; central Catania is packed.

recurringHolidays.name: Festino di Santa Rosalia (Palermo)
recurringHolidays.effect: Palermo's street festival with fireworks; hotels busy.

recurringHolidays.name: Ferragosto
recurringHolidays.effect: Ferry and car-hire prices peak; beaches overflow.

prices.notes: Costa Smeralda is luxury-priced in July–August. Car-hire rates in Sardinia can triple in August, so book months ahead.

countries.name: Kosovo
countries.summary: Kosovo is young and welcoming. Prishtina, Prizren and the Rugova mountains are best from May to October. Summer brings the diaspora home and festivals such as Dokufest in Prizren. Winter is cold, with smog in the capital, and skiing at Brezovica.
countries.splitReason: Kosovo is a small, landlocked country with one continental calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Prishtina, Prizren, Peja and the Rugova Gorge, Gjakova and Brezovica.

best.why: Green mountains and pleasant city days.
A golden autumn in Rugova.

worst.why: Cold, with smog in Prishtina.

shoulder.why: The diaspora returns: busy, hot and festive (Dokufest in Prizren).

recurringHolidays.name: Dokufest (Prizren)
recurringHolidays.effect: The documentary film festival; Prizren is busy.

prices.notes: Uses the euro, and is very affordable.

countries.name: Latvia
countries.summary: Riga's Art Nouveau streets and the Jūrmala beaches are best in summer, when Midsummer (Jāņi) is the biggest celebration of the year. Spring and autumn are cool, and winter is dark and snowy.
countries.splitReason: Latvia is small and flat, with one Baltic climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Riga, Jūrmala, Sigulda and Gauja National Park, Cēsis, Rundāle and Kurzeme.

best.why: Jūrmala beaches, Riga's Art Nouveau in summer light and Jāņi (Midsummer).

worst.why: Dark, cold and grey.

recurringHolidays.name: Jāņi (Midsummer)
recurringHolidays.effect: Latvia's biggest holiday: shops close and everyone heads to the countryside.

prices.notes: Good value. Riga's old town is pricier than the centre.

countries.name: Liechtenstein
countries.summary: Liechtenstein suits hiking from June to September (the Liechtenstein Trail) and family skiing at Malbun from January to March. It's quiet in the spring and late-autumn in-between seasons.
countries.splitReason: Liechtenstein is a tiny alpine principality with one climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Vaduz, Schaan and the Malbun ski area.

best.why: Hiking the Liechtenstein Trail and the alpine huts.
Family skiing at Malbun.

worst.why: Grey, with little open.

shoulder.why: Spring in the valley, with snow lingering up high.

prices.notes: Uses the Swiss franc, with Swiss price levels. Easy as a day trip from Zurich.

countries.name: Lithuania
countries.summary: Vilnius's baroque old town, Trakai castle and the Curonian Spit's dunes are best from June to August, with white-ish nights and Midsummer (Joninės). Winters are long and cold.
countries.splitReason: Lithuania is small and flat, with one Baltic climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Vilnius, Trakai, Kaunas, Klaipėda, the Curonian Spit and Palanga.

best.why: The Curonian Spit's dunes, terraces in Vilnius's old town and Midsummer (Joninės).

worst.why: Dark and cold, with icy streets.

prices.notes: Good value. Nida on the Curonian Spit books out in July.

countries.name: Luxembourg
countries.summary: Luxembourg has a mild continental climate. Summer and early autumn suit hiking in the Mullerthal and Moselle wine tours; winter is grey, with Christmas markets.
countries.splitReason: Luxembourg is a tiny country with one climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Luxembourg City, Vianden, the Mullerthal and the Moselle valley.

best.why: Green valleys and warm days for the Mullerthal trail.
The Moselle wine harvest and golden forests.

worst.why: Cold, grey and damp.

shoulder.why: Warm, with locals away on holiday.

prices.notes: Public transport is free nationwide. City hotels are business-priced on weekdays.

countries.name: Malta
countries.summary: Malta is sunny almost all year. Spring and autumn (into November) are ideal for history, diving and swimming. Summer is hot, humid and busy, and winter is mild (16 °C) with rainy spells, good for Valletta and the Neolithic temples.
countries.splitReason: Malta is a small archipelago with one Mediterranean climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Malta, Gozo and Comino.

best.why: Warm, sunny and green, with the sea warming up.
Sea at 23–25 °C, great diving and the village festas winding down.

worst.why: Hot (32 °C), humid and crowded.

shoulder.why: A mild 16 °C winter, great for history, with rainy spells.
The sea is at its warmest.

recurringHolidays.name: Village festas
recurringHolidays.effect: Fireworks and processions; lively but noisy.

recurringHolidays.name: Carnival
recurringHolidays.effect: Valletta parades.

prices.notes: Good value in winter. Book the Hypogeum weeks ahead.

countries.name: Moldova
countries.summary: Moldova is wine country, with vast cellars at Cricova and Mileștii Mici. Visit in late spring or during the September–October harvest, when National Wine Day falls in early October. Winters are cold and grey.
countries.splitReason: Moldova is small and landlocked, with one continental calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Chișinău, the Cricova and Mileștii Mici wine cellars, Orheiul Vechi and Soroca.

best.why: Green countryside and pleasant warmth.
The wine harvest and National Wine Day (early October).

worst.why: Cold and grey, with few visitors.

recurringHolidays.name: National Wine Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Wine festival in Chișinău.

prices.notes: Very cheap. Check advice before visiting Transnistria.

countries.name: Monaco
countries.summary: Monaco has the Riviera's mild climate: sunny summers and gentle 13 °C winters. Spring and early autumn are ideal. The Grand Prix week in late May sends prices sky-high.
countries.splitReason: Monaco is a tiny city-state with one Riviera climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Monte Carlo, Monaco-Ville, La Condamine and Fontvieille.

best.why: Sunny 18–24 °C days for the gardens and harbour.
Warm sea and calmer streets.

worst.why: Peak crowds and prices.

shoulder.why: Mild winters, with the Monte-Carlo Rally in January.

recurringHolidays.name: Monaco Grand Prix
recurringHolidays.effect: Hotel prices increase fivefold, with roads closed.

prices.notes: Stay in Nice or Menton and visit by train.

countries.name: Montenegro
countries.summary: Montenegro's Bay of Kotor and Budva beaches shine from late spring to early autumn, while Durmitor's mountains are a summer hiking and rafting destination. July–August is crowded and expensive. Winters on the coast are among Europe's wettest.
countries.splitReason: Montenegro is small, and the coast and Durmitor mountains share one calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Kotor and its bay, Budva, Herceg Novi, Ulcinj, Durmitor and the Tara Canyon, and Cetinje.

best.why: A warm sea and calm old towns before the cruise peak.
The sea is still warm, with crowds thinning.

worst.why: Peak crowds in Kotor and Budva, with peak prices.
The coast is among Europe's wettest (2,000+ mm in Kotor), and resorts close.

shoulder.why: Spring, with snow on the peaks.

prices.notes: Stay in Perast or Dobrota to avoid Kotor's cruise crowds.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.summary: The Netherlands is mild, breezy and changeable. Mid-April brings the tulip fields and Keukenhof, and King's Day on April 27 turns Amsterdam orange. June to September is best for canals and cycling. Winter is grey, wet and windy.
countries.splitReason: The Netherlands is small and flat, with one maritime climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The whole country: Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague, Utrecht, Delft, the tulip fields and the North Sea coast.

best.why: Tulip season at Keukenhof (mid-April) and King's Day (April 27).
Long days and good cycling weather.
Mild, with the summer crowds gone.

worst.why: Grey, wet, windy and dark by 4:30 pm.

recurringHolidays.name: King's Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Amsterdam's biggest party: hotels are full.

recurringHolidays.name: Keukenhof season
recurringHolidays.effect: The famous tulip gardens; book timed tickets.

prices.notes: Amsterdam has a high tourist tax and expensive hotels; Rotterdam and Utrecht are good bases.

countries.name: North Macedonia
countries.summary: Lake Ohrid is the highlight: swimming from June to early September and quiet beauty in spring and autumn. Skopje is quirky and cheap. Winters are cold, with heavy smog in Skopje.
countries.splitReason: North Macedonia is small and landlocked, with one continental calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Skopje, Ohrid, Bitola, the Matka Canyon and Mavrovo.

best.why: Warm days at Lake Ohrid before the summer crowds.
A calm lake and a mild autumn.

worst.why: Cold, with severe smog in Skopje.

shoulder.why: The Ohrid Summer Festival and busy lake beaches.
Cooling, with the first smog days.

risks.note: Skopje and Tetovo have some of Europe's worst winter smog.

prices.notes: Very cheap. Ohrid books up in August.

countries.name: Norway
countries.summary: Norway splits into the fjord country of the south-west and the Arctic north. The fjords are a June–August destination, when ferries run, mountain roads such as Trollstigen are open and hikes like Trolltunga are possible. North of the Arctic Circle, summer brings the midnight sun, while January to March is prime northern-lights season with returning daylight. Svalbard, at 78°N, is for polar-bear country expeditions.

regions.name: Fjord Norway & Oslo
regions.description: Oslo, Bergen, the western fjords (Geiranger, Nærøyfjord, Flåm), Stavanger (Preikestolen), Trolltunga, Ålesund, Lillehammer and Trondheim.

best.why: Long light days, fjord ferries and mountain roads open (Trollstigen), and the Trolltunga and Preikestolen hikes.

worst.why: Dark (6 hours of daylight) and wet, with many fjord attractions closed.

shoulder.why: Skiing into April as the fjords reawaken, with fruit blossom in Hardanger in May.
Autumn colours and fewer crowds, with more rain.

risks.note: Bergen gets about 230 days of rain a year.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter
recurringHolidays.effect: Norwegians head to mountain cabins; many shops close Thursday to Monday.

recurringHolidays.name: Constitution Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Parades nationwide; offices are closed.

prices.notes: Very expensive. The Norway in a Nutshell route is popular; book Flåm Railway seats.

regions.name: Arctic Norway
regions.description: Tromsø, Lofoten, Senja, Vesterålen, Alta and Nordkapp.

best.why: Northern lights with returning daylight, dog-sledding and snow-covered Lofoten.
Midnight sun, Lofoten hiking and sea kayaking.

worst.why: Snowmelt: grey and slushy, the aurora season over and too early for hiking.

shoulder.why: Polar night (no sunrise): auroras are visible but there are few daylight activities.
Autumn colours, with the aurora season beginning in September.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter
recurringHolidays.effect: Norwegians head to mountain cabins; many shops close Thursday to Monday.

recurringHolidays.name: Constitution Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Parades nationwide; offices are closed.

prices.notes: Aurora tours cost €100–200. Lofoten rorbu cabins book out in summer and March.

regions.name: Svalbard
regions.description: Longyearbyen and the Svalbard archipelago at 78°N, home to polar bears, glaciers and walrus.

best.why: Sunlit snow: snowmobile and dog-sled expeditions to the glaciers and east coast.
Midnight sun, boat trips to glaciers and wildlife (walrus, reindeer).

worst.why: Polar night: total darkness, −15 °C and few activities.

risks.note: Severe Arctic cold; polar bears mean you can't leave town unescorted without a firearm.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter
recurringHolidays.effect: Norwegians head to mountain cabins; many shops close Thursday to Monday.

recurringHolidays.name: Constitution Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Parades nationwide; offices are closed.

prices.notes: All excursions outside Longyearbyen need a licensed guide.

countries.name: Poland
countries.summary: Poland has warm summers and cold winters. May–June and the 'golden Polish autumn' (September–early October) are ideal for Kraków, Warsaw and Gdańsk. Summer brings Baltic beaches and Tatra hiking, and December brings Christmas markets. January to March is cold and grey, with smog in Kraków, though it's ski season in Zakopane.
countries.splitReason: Poland follows one continental calendar, with the Baltic coast adding summer beaches and the Tatras skiing.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The whole country: Kraków, Warsaw, Gdańsk, Wrocław, Zakopane and the Tatras, the Masurian lakes and the Baltic coast.

best.why: Warm 18–24 °C with beer gardens and green parks.
The golden Polish autumn: mild, sunny and colourful.

worst.why: Cold (−5 °C), grey and smoggy in Kraków.

shoulder.why: Busy summer, with Baltic beaches and Tatra crowds.

risks.note: Winter smog in Kraków and Silesia.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas markets
recurringHolidays.effect: Kraków's main square market.

prices.notes: Good value. Book Auschwitz-Birkenau guided tours online in advance.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.summary: Mainland Portugal has an Atlantic-Mediterranean climate: wet, mild winters and hot, dry summers, with the Algarve the sunniest corner. Spring and early autumn are ideal for Lisbon, Porto and the Douro. Madeira is mild all year, around 19–25 °C. The Azores are greener, wetter and best from June to September.

regions.name: Lisbon, Porto & Central Portugal
regions.description: Lisbon, Sintra and Cascais, Porto, the Douro Valley, Coimbra, Óbidos, Évora and the Alentejo.

best.why: Warm, sunny 20–26 °C days, jacaranda in bloom in Lisbon and the Santo António festivals in June.
The Douro grape harvest and warm, golden days.

worst.why: Peak crowds in Lisbon and Sintra, and 40 °C heat in the Douro.

shoulder.why: Mild but rainy (12–15 °C), cheap and quiet.

recurringHolidays.name: Santo António (Lisbon)
recurringHolidays.effect: Street parties with sardines in Alfama; book ahead.

recurringHolidays.name: São João (Porto)
recurringHolidays.effect: Porto's all-night street festival.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter
recurringHolidays.effect: A domestic travel peak.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year

The sea at its warmest (22 °C), calm and with fewer people.

shoulder.why: Mild, sunny 16–17 °C winters for golf and coastal walks, but too cool to swim.

best.why: Warm and dry: clear levada walks, the spring Flower Festival and a 20–23 °C sea.

shoulder.why: A mild 19 °C winter escape with more showers, and spectacular New Year fireworks.

risks.note: Hillside fires in hot, dry spells.
Downpours can cause landslides on the levadas.

regions.name: Azores
regions.description: São Miguel, Pico, Faial, Terceira and Flores, in the mid-Atlantic.

best.why: The warmest, sunniest months: hydrangeas in bloom, whale and dolphin watching and crater-lake hikes.

worst.why: Wet and windy, with frequent Atlantic storms and limited ferries between islands.

shoulder.why: Spring, when sperm and blue whales migrate past (April–May).

countries.name: Romania
countries.summary: Romania's Transylvanian towns and Carpathian scenery are best from late spring to mid-autumn. The spectacular Transfăgărășan road opens only from July to October, and the Danube Delta's birdlife peaks in May–June. Winter brings snowy villages and skiing at Poiana Brașov.
countries.splitReason: Transylvania, Bucharest, the Danube Delta and the coast follow one continental calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The whole country: Transylvania (Brașov, Sibiu, Sighișoara, Bran), Bucharest, the Carpathians, Maramureș, Bucovina, the Danube Delta and the Black Sea.

best.why: Green Carpathians, with the Danube Delta's birdlife at its peak (May–June).
A golden Transylvanian autumn, with the Transfăgărășan still open.

worst.why: The thaw: muddy and grey, with mountain roads closed.

shoulder.why: Skiing at Poiana Brașov and Christmas markets.
A busy Black Sea coast and the Transfăgărășan open.

risks.note: The Transfăgărășan and Transalpina are closed.

prices.notes: Good value. Driving is the best way to explore the villages.

countries.name: Russia
countries.summary: Many governments, including the UK's, advise against all travel to Russia, so check current advice. Seasonally, Moscow and St Petersburg are best from late May to mid-July (St Petersburg's White Nights) and in the brief golden autumn. Sochi is a subtropical summer resort with winter skiing nearby. Lake Baikal is spectacular when frozen (February–March) and in summer. Kamchatka's volcanoes and bears are a July–September expedition.

regions.name: Moscow, St Petersburg & the Golden Ring
regions.description: Moscow, St Petersburg, the Golden Ring towns (Suzdal, Vladimir) and Kazan.

best.why: St Petersburg's White Nights (late May to mid-July) and lush Moscow parks.
A brief golden autumn.

worst.why: Dark, snowy and −10 °C, with slush.

recurringHolidays.name: May holidays

regions.name: Sochi & the Caucasus
regions.description: Sochi, Krasnaya Polyana and Rosa Khutor, Mt Elbrus and Dombay.

best.why: Warm sea and mountain meadows in bloom.
A warm sea into October.

worst.why: Rainy, with the ski season not yet started.

recurringHolidays.name: New Year holidays

recurringHolidays.name: May holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: A domestic travel peak.

regions.name: Lake Baikal & Siberia
regions.description: Lake Baikal (Listvyanka, Olkhon), Irkutsk, the Altai, Novosibirsk, Yekaterinburg and the Trans-Siberian railway.

best.why: Baikal's clear blue ice: drive, skate and hike on the frozen lake.
Warm summer for Olkhon, Altai treks and the Trans-Siberian.

worst.why: Ice break-up: the lake is unsafe and roads are muddy.
Freezing, but Baikal isn't walkable yet.

shoulder.why: Deep cold (−25 °C) as the ice forms.

regions.name: Kamchatka & the Far East
regions.description: Kamchatka (volcanoes, bears, the Valley of Geysers), Vladivostok and Sakhalin.

best.why: Volcano treks, brown bears at Kurile Lake and the Valley of Geysers by helicopter.

worst.why: Deep snow and storms, with most excursions closed.

recurringHolidays.name: New Year holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Russia's longest holiday: transport and resorts are busy.

recurringHolidays.name: May holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: A domestic travel peak.

regions.name: Murmansk, Karelia & the Arctic
regions.description: Murmansk, Teriberka, the Kola Peninsula, Karelia (Kizhi) and Arkhangelsk.

best.why: Northern lights over Teriberka's icy coast.
Midnight sun and Kizhi island in Karelia.

worst.why: Snowmelt slush, with the aurora season over.

recurringHolidays.name: New Year holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Russia's longest holiday: transport and resorts are busy.

recurringHolidays.name: May holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: A domestic travel peak.

prices.notes: Aurora tours from Murmansk cost about €60–120.

countries.name: San Marino
aliases: Most Serene Republic of San Marino
countries.summary: San Marino sits atop Monte Titano near Rimini. It's best in spring and early autumn; summer brings Riviera day-trippers and winter is cold and foggy.
countries.splitReason: San Marino is a tiny hilltop republic with one climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The City of San Marino on Monte Titano and Borgo Maggiore.

best.why: Clear views to the Adriatic in mild weather.
Pleasant autumn days.

worst.why: Cold and foggy, with many shops quiet.

shoulder.why: Hot and busy with day-trippers from Rimini.
Chilly late autumn, with Christmas markets.

prices.notes: Usually visited as a day trip; staying overnight gives you quiet evenings.

countries.name: Serbia
countries.summary: Belgrade is lively all year, with river clubs in summer and cosy kafanas in winter. Spring and early autumn are most comfortable. July brings the EXIT festival in Novi Sad and hot weather. Winter is cold and windy, with skiing at Kopaonik.
countries.splitReason: Serbia is landlocked, with one continental calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Belgrade, Novi Sad, Niš, Zlatibor, Tara National Park and Kopaonik.

best.why: Warm, green days with Belgrade's river terraces opening.
Mild autumn and the wine harvest.

worst.why: Cold, with biting Košava winds.

shoulder.why: Hot (30 °C+), with the EXIT festival and lively river clubs.

recurringHolidays.name: EXIT Festival (Novi Sad)
recurringHolidays.effect: Novi Sad sells out.

recurringHolidays.name: Orthodox Christmas
recurringHolidays.effect: Family holiday.

prices.notes: Very good value. Belgrade's nightlife is legendary.

countries.name: Slovakia
countries.summary: Slovakia's High Tatras have strict seasons: the high trails open from June 16 to October 31, and skiing runs from December to March at Jasná and the Tatras. Bratislava and the castles are best in late spring and early autumn.
countries.splitReason: Slovakia is small and shares one continental calendar, with the Tatras setting the mountain seasons.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Bratislava, the High and Low Tatras, Slovak Paradise, Banská Štiavnica and Spiš Castle.

best.why: The High Tatras' upper trails reopen on June 16.
Clear autumn hiking with fewer people.
Green valleys and castles, with the lower trails open.

worst.why: Mud season: skiing is over and the high trails are closed.

shoulder.why: Ski season at Jasná and in the Tatras.
Spring with snow lingering up high.
Peak Tatras hiking, busy at weekends.
High trails close on November 1; grey early winter.

prices.notes: Mountain chalets (chaty) need booking for summer weekends.

countries.name: Slovenia
countries.summary: Slovenia packs the Julian Alps, Lake Bled, the emerald Soča and a sliver of Adriatic coast into a tiny area. Late spring and September are ideal; July and August are busy at Bled. November is the wettest month, and winter brings skiing at Kranjska Gora and Vogel.
countries.splitReason: Slovenia is small, and the Alps, Ljubljana, the Karst and the coast share one calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The whole country: Ljubljana, Bled, Bohinj and the Julian Alps, the Soča valley, the Karst caves and Piran.

best.why: Lake Bled and the Julian Alps are green, the Soča is emerald and days are 22–26 °C.
Clear autumn, the wine harvest and fewer crowds at Bled.

worst.why: The wettest month: foggy and grey.

shoulder.why: Skiing at Kranjska Gora and Vogel; Christmas lights in Ljubljana.
Spring, with snow lingering up high.
Bled is packed, with afternoon storms.

prices.notes: Bled accommodation peaks in summer. The Vršič pass is open from about May to October.

countries.name: Spain
countries.summary: Spain has several climates. Green Spain in the north is mild and rainy. The central meseta (Madrid) has hot summers and cold winters. Andalusia has scorching summers but delightful 17 °C winters, and the Mediterranean coast and Balearics are classic summer beach country. The Canary Islands, off Africa, have 'eternal spring' all year. For most of the mainland, spring (April–June) and autumn (September–October) beat midsummer, when August is Spain's holiday month and inland cities hit 40 °C.

regions.name: Green Spain (North Coast)
regions.description: The Basque Country (San Sebastián, Bilbao), Navarre, Cantabria, Asturias (Picos de Europa), Galicia (Santiago de Compostela) and the Camino de Santiago.

best.why: Green Spain at its sunniest: 22–25 °C, beaches at San Sebastián, hikes in the Picos de Europa and good Camino walking.
Warm sea, pintxos season and fewer crowds.

worst.why: A rainy, grey Atlantic winter.

shoulder.why: Peak Spanish holidays: busy beaches and higher prices, but a pleasant 25 °C escape from the southern heat.

regions.name: Madrid & Central Spain
regions.description: Madrid, Toledo, Segovia, Salamanca, Ávila, Zaragoza and Extremadura: the high central plateau.

best.why: Warm 20–28 °C: café terraces, the Retiro park and day trips to Toledo and Segovia.
Golden autumn and the grape harvest in Ribera del Duero.

worst.why: Madrid at 35–40 °C; many locals leave and some restaurants close in August.

shoulder.why: Cold, crisp and sunny winter, with Christmas lights and great museums.
Getting hot, with lively summer nights.

A warm sea on the Costa del Sol and comfortable sightseeing.

worst.why: Seville and Córdoba hit 40–45 °C, among Europe's hottest cities; only sightsee early or late.

shoulder.why: Mild, sunny 16–18 °C winter (Europe's best winter city-break region), with skiing in the Sierra Nevada.
Hot, with beach season in full swing.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas to Reyes

The sea is at its warmest, with the La Mercè festival and crowds easing.

regions.name: Balearic Islands

The sea at 25 °C, softer light and crowds thinning.

worst.why: Peak crowds and prices: Ibiza's club season peak and the busiest beaches.
Resorts and many restaurants are closed, though Palma stays lively.

shoulder.why: The cycling season, with almond blossom, but a cool sea.
A very warm sea, with crowds easing.

recurringHolidays.effect: Family holidays; the Three Kings parades on Jan 5.

regions.name: Canary Islands
regions.description: Tenerife, Gran Canaria, Lanzarote, Fuerteventura, La Palma and La Gomera, off the coast of West Africa.

best.why: 'Eternal spring': 22–26 °C all winter, making it Europe's top winter-sun escape, with hikes up Teide.

shoulder.why: Warm and breezy with a 21–23 °C sea; Spanish family holidays in August and occasional calima dust haze.

risks.note: Calima: Saharan dust haze can ground flights for a day or two.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas to Reyes
recurringHolidays.effect: Family holidays; the Three Kings parades on Jan 5.

prices.notes: Winter is the high season (December–March) and the best value comes in May–June. The Teide summit needs a free permit booked weeks ahead.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.summary: Sweden's south (Stockholm, Gothenburg, Gotland) shines from June to August, with long light days, archipelago swims and Midsummer. Lapland in the far north offers the Icehotel, northern lights and dog-sledding from January to March, and midnight-sun hiking in summer. Winters in the south are dark and slushy.

regions.name: Stockholm & Southern Sweden
regions.description: Stockholm and its archipelago, Gothenburg, Malmö and Skåne, Uppsala, Gotland, Öland and Dalarna.

best.why: Long light days, archipelago swimming and Midsummer (around June 20–26).

worst.why: Dark (6 hours of daylight), cold and slushy.

shoulder.why: Lengthening days, with spring blossom in May.

recurringHolidays.name: Midsummer
recurringHolidays.effect: Swedes leave the cities and many shops close.

recurringHolidays.name: Industrial holiday
recurringHolidays.effect: The domestic travel peak; city offices empty.

regions.name: Lapland & the North
regions.description: Kiruna, Abisko, the Jukkasjärvi Icehotel, Luleå and the Åre ski area.

best.why: Northern lights, the Icehotel and dog-sledding as the daylight returns.
Midnight sun and hiking the Kungsleden.

worst.why: Snowmelt mud, with the aurora season over.

shoulder.why: Ruska autumn colours (early September) and the first auroras.
Polar night in December and deep cold; the Icehotel opens in December.

recurringHolidays.name: Midsummer
recurringHolidays.effect: Swedes leave the cities and many shops close.

recurringHolidays.name: Industrial holiday
recurringHolidays.effect: The domestic travel peak; city offices empty.

prices.notes: The Icehotel's cold rooms cost €300+ a night. Abisko has some of the clearest aurora skies.

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.summary: Switzerland is a two-season destination: skiing from December to April (Zermatt, Verbier, St. Moritz) and the alpine summer from late June to September, when the high passes, mountain railways and huts are open. Spring and November are in-between months, when many lifts close for maintenance. It's Europe's most expensive country.
countries.splitReason: Switzerland is a compact alpine country whose valleys and peaks share one calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The whole country: Zurich, Geneva, Lucerne, the Jungfrau region, Zermatt, the Engadin, Ticino and Lake Geneva.

best.why: Ski season with reliable snow and sunny days.
The summer Alps: Jungfrau and Matterhorn hikes, the lakes and Glacier Express views.

worst.why: Between seasons: grey, with many lifts and mountain hotels closed.

shoulder.why: Christmas markets and the ski season opening at peak prices.
Green valleys, but the high passes stay closed until June and lifts close for maintenance.

risks.note: High passes (Furka, Grimsel, Susten) are closed.

recurringHolidays.name: Swiss National Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Fireworks and bonfires.

prices.notes: Europe's priciest country. The Swiss Travel Pass covers trains, boats and museums.

countries.name: Ukraine
countries.summary: Ukraine is at war, and many governments advise against all travel, so check current advice. In normal times, Kyiv and Lviv are best in late spring and early autumn, the Carpathians in summer (hiking) and winter (skiing at Bukovel), and Odesa's coast in summer.
countries.splitReason: Ukraine follows one continental calendar; the Carpathians add skiing and hiking.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Kyiv, Lviv, Odesa, Chernivtsi and the Carpathians.

best.why: Chestnut blossom in Kyiv and green parks.
Golden autumn days in Kyiv and Lviv.

worst.why: Cold and snowy (−5 °C).

prices.notes: Wartime conditions mean insurance, flights and security all need checking.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.summary: Britain's maritime climate is mild and changeable all year, rarely very hot or very cold. Late spring and early summer bring the most sunshine and long light evenings (until 10 pm in Scotland), and September is often settled and quieter. Winter is short, grey and damp, but London's Christmas lights and Edinburgh's Hogmanay are highlights. School summer holidays (late July–August) push up prices, and Highland midges peak from June to August.

regions.name: England & Wales
regions.description: London, Oxford, Cambridge, Bath, the Cotswolds, Cornwall and Devon, the Lake District, York, the Peak District and Wales (Cardiff, Snowdonia).

best.why: Long light evenings, gardens in bloom and 17–22 °C days, with the Chelsea Flower Show in May and Wimbledon from late June.
Often warm and settled, and quieter after the school holidays.

worst.why: Dark (sunset around 4 pm), damp and grey, though the Christmas lights and markets brighten things.

shoulder.why: Daffodils and longer days, but showery.
Warm but unpredictable; the busiest and priciest weeks with school holidays.

risks.note: Atlantic storms bring flooding and travel disruption.

recurringHolidays.name: Notting Hill Carnival
recurringHolidays.effect: West London is packed.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter bank-holiday weekend
recurringHolidays.effect: Busy roads and attractions.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Almost everything closes on December 25, and trains are reduced.

prices.notes: London is very expensive, and regional towns are better value. Prices are converted from GBP.

regions.name: Scotland & Northern Ireland
regions.description: Edinburgh, Glasgow, the Highlands (Inverness, Loch Ness, Glencoe, Ben Nevis), the Isle of Skye, the Cairngorms, Orkney and Northern Ireland (Belfast, the Giant's Causeway).

best.why: The driest, sunniest spell, with long evenings before the midges peak.
Autumn colours, with fewer midges and crowds.

worst.why: Short, dark days (about 7 hours of light) and gales disrupting Highland roads and ferries.

shoulder.why: Snow on the peaks, getting lighter.
A busy summer: Edinburgh's Festival in August triples prices, and Highland midges are out.

risks.note: Gales cancel ferries to the islands.

recurringHolidays.name: Edinburgh Festival Fringe
recurringHolidays.effect: The world's largest arts festival: hotels triple in price.

recurringHolidays.name: Hogmanay
recurringHolidays.effect: Edinburgh's street party; book early.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter bank-holiday weekend
recurringHolidays.effect: Busy roads and attractions.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Almost everything closes on December 25, and trains are reduced.

prices.notes: Book Skye accommodation months ahead for summer. Prices are converted from GBP.

countries.name: Vatican City
countries.summary: The Vatican shares Rome's climate. Crowds, not weather, are the main issue: Easter, Christmas and the summer bring the longest queues for St Peter's and the Sistine Chapel. January to early March and late autumn are quietest.
countries.splitReason: Vatican City is the world's smallest state, entirely within Rome.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: St Peter's Basilica and Square, the Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel.

best.why: The shortest queues at the Vatican Museums, on mild, sunny days.
Autumn with fewer crowds.

worst.why: Hot, with very long queues for the Sistine Chapel and St Peter's.

shoulder.why: A busy spring with Easter pilgrims and school groups.
Christmas: Midnight Mass and papal-blessing crowds.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter
recurringHolidays.effect: Papal Easter masses pack St Peter's Square.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas
recurringHolidays.effect: Midnight Mass and the Urbi et Orbi blessing.

prices.notes: Book Vatican Museums tickets online. Entry is free on the last Sunday of the month, but queues are huge.
